title: 石喷泉旁边  (By the Stone Fountain)

segments.t: Clear water trickles gently into the carved stone basin on Wutong Lane. Qing and Hao compare the watercolour card with the stone rim while Manager Zhou peers eagerly down a narrow side lane. Let us listen in first.
看水彩卡片的左边——画着一片小小的树叶！
小晴，绕着水池干的那一边走，石头上看得见吗？
就在水嘴底下！一片石头树叶指着西北边的斜坡！
我来念第二张卡片：跟着树叶走，直到十二声钟声拉出直影子。
十二声钟声！那肯定是往上三个街口的老市政钟楼！
顺着大街走三个街口？胡说，我知道一条两分钟的近路！
周经理，您确定走这条窄巷子吗？我的指南针说它往南拐。
志豪，我在梧桐巷住了二十年，巷子比指南针管用！
周经理，您选这个路口以前，记得把老花镜拉下来了吗？
认一条笔直的街坊巷子，谁还用老花镜呀？
行，请队长带队吧，我在笔记本上记下每一次拐弯。
过了花盆往左拐，过了绿栅栏又往左拐——我们到底去哪儿呀？！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
看水彩卡片的左边——画着一片小小的树叶！
'Look at the left side of the watercolour sketch—there is a tiny carved leaf!' "Shuicai" literally pairs "water" and "colour" for watercolour paint, and "pian" counts flat thin things like leaves.
小晴，绕着水池干的那一边走，石头上看得见吗？
'Walk around the dry side of the basin, Qing; do you see it on the stone?' inserting "de" inside "kan de jian" builds "able to see", and first-tone "gan" means "dry" rather than fourth-tone "do".
就在水嘴底下！一片石头树叶指着西北边的斜坡！

'Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!' "Shui zui" literally says "water mouth" for a fountain spout, and Mandarin reverses "northwest" into "xibei", "west-north".
我来念第二张卡片：跟着树叶走，直到十二声钟声拉出直影子。
'Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.' "Zhidao" means "right up until", while "zhongsheng" pairs "bell" and "sound" for the chimes of a tower clock.
十二声钟声！那肯定是往上三个街口的老市政钟楼！
'Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!' Confident "kending" means "for sure" or "has to be", and "zhonglou" literally joins "bell" and "tower".
顺着大街走三个街口？胡说，我知道一条两分钟的近路！

'Three blocks up the main street? Nonsense, I know a two-minute shortcut!' "Jinlu" literally says "near-road" for a shortcut, counted with "tiao", Mandarin's go-to counter for winding streets and lanes.
周经理，您确定走这条窄巷子吗？我的指南针说它往南拐。

'Are you sure about this narrow lane, Manager Zhou? My compass says that bends south.' "Xiangzi" means a narrow neighbourhood alley, and "wang nan guai" pictures the lane veering off "toward the south".
志豪，我在梧桐巷住了二十年，巷子比指南针管用！

'I have lived on Wutong Lane for twenty years, Hao, and alleys beat compasses!' Comparison in Mandarin needs no special ending: "xiangzi bi zhinanzhen guanyong" simply states "alleys compared-to compasses work-better".
周经理，您选这个路口以前，记得把老花镜拉下来了吗？

'Did you remember to pull your reading glasses down before choosing that turn, Manager Zhou?' "Laohua" describes farsighted eyes that blur close print, so "laohuajing" is the everyday name for reading glasses.
认一条笔直的街坊巷子，谁还用老花镜呀？

'Who needs reading glasses to recognize a perfectly straight neighbourhood lane?' Vivid "bizhi" means "brush-straight"—as straight as a calligraphy brush handle—and "shui hai yong" asks "who even needs?".
行，请队长带队吧，我在笔记本上记下每一次拐弯。
'All right, lead the expedition, captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.' Brisk "xing" means "all right, deal", while "bijiben" stacks "brush", "note", and "book" for a pocket notebook.
过了花盆往左拐，过了绿栅栏又往左拐——我们到底去哪儿呀？！
'Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence—where are we going?!' Putting "daodi" ahead of "nar", "where", adds exasperated emphasis: "where on earth are we going?!".
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
看水彩卡片的左边——画着一片小小的树叶！

十二声钟声！那肯定是往上三个街口的老市政钟楼！

行，请队长带队吧，我在笔记本上记下每一次拐弯。
过了花盆往左拐，过了绿栅栏又往左拐——我们到底去哪儿呀？！
Ignoring both the brass compass and his own reading glasses, Manager Zhou marches everyone proudly down a winding side alley. See you next time.
下次见！
